claims.text: The as-deposited FeNiCrCoCu thin film has a homogeneous elemental distribution.
The as-deposited FeNiCrCoCu thin film has a nanoscale grain structure.
Controlled annealing promotes Cu diffusion and segregation relative to the as-deposited coating.
Elevated temperature increases atomic mobility in FeNiCrCoCu.
Enhanced atomic mobility drives Cu out of the solid solution and toward grain boundaries and wear surfaces.
Cu segregation produces a Cu-enriched nanolayer at the wear interface and along grain boundaries.
The Cu-enriched nanolayer is oxidatively stable during high-temperature sliding.
The Cu-enriched nanolayer is lubricious during sliding wear.
The Cu-enriched nanolayer reduces friction under high load.
The Cu-enriched nanolayer reduces plastic deformation under high load.
Reduced friction and plastic deformation improve the overall wear resistance of the coating.
Pre-annealed coatings will have a lower wear rate than as-deposited coatings under otherwise identical high-temperature, high-load sliding conditions.
Pre-annealed coatings will have a lower coefficient of friction than as-deposited coatings under otherwise identical high-temperature, high-load sliding conditions.
TEM and EDS mapping will reveal Cu enrichment at grain boundaries and the wear interface in pre-annealed coatings.
Atomic diffusion relevant to the proposed mechanism becomes significant above approximately 600°C.
The proposed mechanism applies under high mechanical loading but may not apply under light loads or at lower temperatures.
Protective oxide formation may also contribute to wear resistance.
